newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction sought from Aramco.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction sought from Aramco.

text.p: Gasoline was actively traded lower on Thursday but most traders were sidelined waiting for firmer direction from Saudi Aramco's gasoline import tender.

A European major offered all three high octane unleaded grades and sold 92-octane at $28.40 per barrel fob April 7-11 lifting, 95-octane at $28.50 for April 2-6 and 97-octane at $29.30 for March 28-April 1.
"Just a 10 cent difference between 95 and 92 is ridiculous," said one trader. The spread is usually 70-90 cents per barrel.
But some traders said the outright traded levels were too low as fundamentals in the first-half April were still tight to balanced.
But the second half of April would depend on Taiwan's import tender which closes next Tuesday and Saudi Aramco's buy tender for up to 1.5 million barrels for April.
Offers into Aramco's tender were valid up to March 12, but by Thursday, participants still had not heard any results.
In the longer term, Pakistan's tender which seeks 25,000 tonnes in May and the same quantity in June, should give support. Offers have to be submitted by March 31 and should be valid until April 5.
High offers in its tender for second quarter purchases prompted Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources to invite fresh bids for 80 and 87-octane gasoline.
Pakistan had received offers of $30 per tonne over Mideast naphtha quotes c-and-f, nearly double its premium of $16.745 per tonne it paid for first quarter purchases, sources said.
Naphtha April swaps firmed by 30 cents per barrel to $23.25/$23.40, while May rose 40 cents to $22.70/$22.90.
Traders said the market would be well-supported in April and May while Japanese refiners are shut for maintenance turnarounds.
Strong North Asian demand was evidenced by the purely Japanese-related awards in the Indian naphtha sales tenders since November, a trader said.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is offering by tender a 25,000-tonne cargo of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) from Vizag on the east coast, industry sources said. The tender for the March 30-April 1 lifting, closes March 13 and is valid for a day.
IOC's last Vizag LAN sale, for February 9-11 lifting, was made at the end of January at a $30.00 discount to Japanese spot quotes.
